Liberation provides the ultimate exit.","madhyamaka":"Phala (fruit) ceases at two boundaries: (1) Nirodha/nirvāṇa (extinction) — the complete cessation of karmic ripening through the elimination of root causes (ignorance, craving). (2) Maraṇa (death) — the end of this life's specific fruits, though nonexpired potentials carry forward to the next life unless nirvana is attained.","quantum":"System boundaries: quantum processes have boundaries — decoherence, measurement, system termination. Like karmic fruit: the process operates within boundaries (nirvana = system reset; death = phase boundary). Nothing runs infinitely without boundary conditions.","bridge":"Both quantum processes and karmic ripening operate within boundaries. QM: measurement/decoherence ends the quantum process. Karma: nirvana/death ends the ripening process. Both: processes have natural boundaries that limit their scope.","accessible":"Your past actions produce consequences, but those consequences don't run forever. They end either when you achieve enlightenment (nirvana — total freedom) or when you die (death — end of this chapter). Death doesn't end ALL karma (unexpired potentials carry forward), but it ends THIS life's specific fruits.","twoTruths":"Conventionally, karmic fruit ceases at nirvana or death. Ultimately, fruit, cessation, nirvana, and death are all empty. But the empty process of cessation functions conventionally — liberation IS possible, and each life has a natural ending.","commonMisconception":"NOT saying death ends ALL karma.
